checks.name: Stage clarity
checks.note: All seven stages state one responsibility and name an output file. Stage 07 pairs the compliance check with export, but its outputs are named and the split is justified.

checks.name: Input/output chain
checks.note: Every input traces to the user (call text, notes, partner details), shared onboarding data (org profile), or an earlier stage's output. Stage 06 reads only outputs from 01 and 03.

checks.name: Shared context identified
checks.note: organization-profile.md and plain-language-rules.md are listed separately with the stages that use them. The per-run checklist is explicitly marked as not shared.

checks.name: Variable coverage
checks.note: All five group-specific details named by the user (org name, mission, service area, past grants, board chair) are SCREAMING_SNAKE placeholders. Per-run items are correctly kept out of the placeholder list.

checks.name: Reference rules
checks.note: Placeholder and conditional syntax are correct and wrap a whole section. The LibreOffice guide sits in the stage's references folder, names are lowercase-hyphen, and there are no em dashes. Checkpoints and audits appear on the creative stages.

reason: The map is thorough and passes every check. It falls short of ready-to-use for three reasons: the checkpoint was assumed approved instead of actually presented, skill discovery was skipped, and no follow-up questions were asked. These are process gaps, but they matter in a conversational discovery stage.

checks.name: Check coverage
checks.note: All 13 checks are reported, each with first-run and after-fix status.

checks.name: Call accuracy
checks.note: Most calls hold up. The report missed real issues in stage 07's checkpoint table: it references 'After Step 3', but Process step 4 is the checkpoint, and the checkpoint is conditional. It also missed that stage 01's checkpoint table says 'After Step 4' while the checkpoint is step 5, which is defensible but loosely consistent. More important, the stage 07 audit runs after export and saving, which conflicts with Pattern 12; the report waves this through without fixing step order. CLAUDE.md lists a 'setup/' entry pointing to the questionnaire, which the report handles. It also missed stage 03, where step 6 says repeat 'steps 4 to 6' and the checkpoint table lists 5, which is consistent. Overall the calls are mostly right, but at least one real item (stage 07 audit order relative to the save) is accepted rather than flagged.

checks.name: Reference rules
checks.note: No em dashes. The fixes follow the stage-contract shape, one-way references, the placeholder rules and the naming rules. The headless explanation was added per Pattern 7.

reason: A thorough, well-evidenced report with sensible fixes, but it accepts stage 07's post-export audit order instead of flagging it under Pattern 12.

checks.name: Check coverage
checks.note: All 13 process checks have a section with a first-run result and an after-fix result. Check 9 is marked N/A with a reason.

checks.name: Call accuracy
checks.note: Several calls are wrong or inconsistent. (a) Issue 6.1 says stage 04 restates the timestamp formula, but the same kind of restatement elsewhere is left in place. Stage 01 step 5 still says 'with a source link for every claim', which now conflicts with the revised '(unverified)' audit rule. (b) Stage 04 still points to 03-cut-list/input, so it reads a stage 03 folder; the report accepts this without comment. (c) Stage 01's checkpoint is listed as 'after step 6', but the checkpoint itself is step 7. The report says the step is valid and does not flag the mismatch. (d) The stage 02 fix removed the only place in that stage telling the user where to put the transcript. Arguably fine, since CLAUDE.md still holds the path, but stage 04's read of 03/input is never questioned. (e) Check 13 finds no jargon, yet terms like 'composition' and 'slug' were not examined closely. The stage 01 step 5 inconsistency is the clearest missed violation.

checks.name: Reference rules
checks.note: Fixes follow conventions: one-way references, conditionals wrap whole sections, there are no em dashes, the questionnaire is shipped flat with defaults, and setup guides now have a description and a verification step.

reason: A thorough, well-structured report with sound fixes. It misses that stage 01 step 5 now conflicts with its revised audit rule, and that the stage 01 checkpoint numbering does not line up.
